purpose: Document wearable and carried accessory props by family, status tier, style, visible anatomy, attachment logic, geometry terms, Blender tool IDs, drawing UI tags, source fields, operator checks, and lore hooks.

accessory_status_tiers.social_read: Camp, dungeon, servant, workshop, and improvised accessories.
Everyday townsfolk, tavern, market, kitchen, and travel wear.
Craft identity, merchant counters, workshop ownership, and professional tools.
Visible wealth, trade identity, locked pouches, tidy travel bags, and polished hardware.
Rank, courtly fashion, heraldry, jewelry, expensive closures, and refined personal objects.
Sacred, magical, scholarly, oath, seal, relic, and puzzle-object accessories.
Weapon suspension, guard keys, belt hardware, scabbards, and rank markers.
Portable, patched, concealed, stolen, travel-worn, or multi-use accessories.
Broken, corroded, waterlogged, stripped, abandoned, or reused accessories.

accessory_families.core_function: Hold clothing, armor, pouches, tools, and weapons while advertising status through buckle and strap detail.
Carry coins, herbs, documents, tools, travel goods, or hidden items.
Show rank, belief, faction, wealth, and garment closure through small metal or gem objects.
Mark access, ownership, guard duty, and puzzle logic through key shape, ring, wards, and tags.
Suspend tools, keys, seals, purses, and household implements from a belt or chain.
Attach weapon sheaths and scabbards to belt or harness without modeling the whole weapon system.
Carry, protect, or identify small learned, ritual, or administrative tools.
Hold liquid or travel supplies as body-worn props and room clutter.

source_support.label: V&A fashion accessories
source_support.support_summary: Supports accessories as wearable objects including belts, bags, gloves, fans, and related fashion objects.

source_support.label: The Met collection, belt buckle references
source_support.support_summary: Supports visible buckle, plate, and metal fitting reference variety.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: small pin crossing the buckle frame
small strap loop holding excess belt

craft_sequence: Draw strap width, length, and closure end.
Place buckle frame, tongue, keeper loop, and rivets as separate named parts.
Cut or darken belt holes in a stable ordered row.
Use status/style to switch plain iron, polished brass, or corroded hardware.
Declare attachment sockets for pouches, scabbards, or key hooks.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The belt is the parent accessory socket: other small props hang from loops, hooks, straps, or riveted plates.
operator_checks: Can the buckle be selected apart from the strap?
Are belt holes ordered?
Are attachment sockets explicit for later pouches or scabbards?

lore_book_hooks.book_title: The Belt Carries More Than Cloth
lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names strap, buckle frame, tongue, keeper loop, holes, and attachment sockets.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: A belt is a map of what its wearer expects to need.

source_support.label: The Met collection, purse references
source_support.support_summary: Supports visible purse and pouch reference variety including frames, closures, and decorated small bags.

source_support.label: Britannica handbag
source_support.support_summary: Supports small carried bags as accessories for money and personal items.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: cord loop around neck or mouth
attachment loop on back or top

craft_sequence: Build a soft rounded or folded body outline.
Add flap, mouth/drawstring, belt loop, and closure as named details.
Place stitch lines along visible seams with simple repeated marks.
Use status tiers to switch clean merchant, common, or patched rogue variants.
Declare contents and pickpocket sockets separately from bag geometry.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The pouch attaches by belt loop or tied cord; gameplay sockets decide whether it is wearable, lootable, or static clutter.
operator_checks: Does it read as a soft container, not a box?
Are attachment and loot sockets separate?
Can patched and merchant variants share the same base body?

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names flap, drawstring, belt loop, stitch line, and loot socket.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: A pouch worn smooth at the mouth has been opened more than its owner admits.

source_support.label: Britannica brooch
source_support.support_summary: Supports brooches as ornamental pins or clasps for garments.

source_support.label: Britannica jewelry
source_support.support_summary: Supports jewelry as personal adornment with status, material, and symbolic roles.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: decorated ends on open brooch frame
long fastening needle crossing the frame
attachment relation to cloak or garment

materials: iron, bronze, silver-like, or gold-like metal
craft_sequence: Build the ring frame first, open or closed.
Add terminals and pin as separate named metal parts.
Use bosses, tiny symbol panels, or gem sockets by style tier.
Use corrosion/damage toggles for ruin variants.
Declare cloth socket separately from the brooch mesh.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The brooch pins through cloth; the visible asset needs a cloth socket and pin orientation even if cloth is not generated.
operator_checks: Does the pin read as a functional clasp?
Can the brooch be worn on cloth or dropped as loot?
Are terminals separate for style variants?

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names frame, terminal, pin, boss, and cloth socket.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: A cloak pin closes cloth, but it opens a history of who wore it.

source_support.label: Britannica ring
source_support.support_summary: Supports rings as personal jewelry and signet/seal-bearing objects.

source_support.label: The Met collection, signet ring references
source_support.support_summary: Supports visible signet ring reference variety with seal faces and metal bands.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: flat or raised face carrying symbol
transition from band to seal face

materials: gold-like, silver-like, bronze, or iron metal
craft_sequence: Build ring band and seal face as separate named forms.
Add shoulders and engraving as shallow relief or dark cut detail.
Use material tier to switch guild bronze, merchant silver, or noble gold.
Keep seal symbol source-owned so Blender does not invent heraldry.
Declare seal/use socket for documents or wax separately.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The ring can be worn, looted, or used as a seal; the seal face is the gameplay-facing detail.
operator_checks: Does the seal face read at prop scale?
Is the symbol sourced outside Blender?
Can the ring become a quest token without changing mesh basics?

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names band, seal face, shoulder, engraving, and identity socket.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: The smallest ring in a room can carry the heaviest authority.

source_support.label: Britannica jewelry
source_support.support_summary: Supports jewelry as personal adornment, status object, and symbolic object.

source_support.label: The Met collection, pendant references
source_support.support_summary: Supports visible pendant reference variety for loops, central faces, gems, and small hanging forms.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: front motif, gem, or relief field

materials: bronze, silver-like, gold-like, stone, cord, chain, gem/enamel optional
craft_sequence: Choose pendant body profile and chain-loop placement.
Add symbol face or gem socket as a source-owned front detail.
Represent cord/chain as simple curve path unless chain links are explicitly requested.
Use style tiers to switch devotional, arcane, noble, or traveler variants.
Declare wearable and inventory sockets separately.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The pendant hangs from cord or chain; front-facing orientation matters for inspection and character wear.
operator_checks: Does the front face have a clear orientation?
Is the symbol source-owned?
Can cord/chain be disabled for dropped loot?

lore_book_hooks.book_title: What Hangs Close to the Heart
lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names pendant body, chain loop, symbol face, cord, and wear socket.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: An amulet is a private argument with fear.

source_support.label: Britannica lock
source_support.support_summary: Supports lock-and-key concepts for access, security, and mechanism vocabulary.

source_support.label: The Met collection, key references
source_support.support_summary: Supports visible key reference variety including bows, shanks, bits, and rings.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: key heads with holes or loops

craft_sequence: Create key ring and key count first.
Build each key from bow, shank, and bit profiles.
Use different bit silhouettes for gameplay identity.
Add optional tag, guild mark, or room label as separate part.
Use corroded variants for abandoned locks and ruins.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: Keys hang from a ring; each key should have a stable identity id so gameplay can map shape to door or chest access.
operator_checks: Can each key be identified separately?
Do bits differ enough to matter?
Is access mapping source-owned?

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names bow, shank, bit, ward cut, key ring, and access id.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: A key is a promise that one shape is allowed where another is not.

source_support.label: The Met collection, chatelaine references
source_support.support_summary: Supports visible chatelaine and hanging accessory reference variety with hooks, chains, and suspended tools.

source_support.label: V&A fashion accessories
source_support.support_summary: Supports wearable accessories as a broad category for hooks, bags, and personal carrying objects.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: top hook or plate that hangs from belt
simple hanging links or curve paths
small rings for tools or keys
attachment points for keys, seals, scissors, or tools

craft_sequence: Build top belt hook and central plate first.
Add chains/rings as separate sockets and simple curves.
Declare each hanging object as a socket, not baked content.
Use guild or noble style to add mark plates or polished bosses.
Keep low-compute variant to hook, plate, and socket markers.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The chatelaine is an accessory socket tree: belt hook -> plate -> chains/rings -> attached small tools.
operator_checks: Are attached tools sockets rather than guessed geometry?
Does the hook clearly attach to a belt?
Can chain count be reduced for low compute?

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names belt hook, hanging plate, chain, split ring, and tool socket.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: The tools at a belt can name a household faster than a sign over the door.

source_support.label: Britannica handbag
source_support.support_summary: Supports carried bags as accessories for personal items and money.

source_support.label: V&A fashion accessories
source_support.support_summary: Supports bags and related objects as fashion/accessory references.

craft_sequence: Block the soft rectangular bag body and gussets.
Add flap and strap as separate named parts.
Place buckle/toggle and stitch lines on the front-facing side.
Use patches, guild tag, or merchant polish by status/style.
Declare content/socket fields for books, letters, tools, or stolen goods.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The satchel can be body-worn by strap or placed as room clutter; contents should be sockets.
operator_checks: Does the strap attach believably?
Are contents sockets, not baked guesses?
Can patches/closures change caste without rebuilding the body?

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names flap, gusset, shoulder strap, closure, and content socket.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: A bag carried across roads wears its truth at the corners.

source_support.label: The Met collection, scabbard references
source_support.support_summary: Supports visible scabbard and weapon suspension reference variety.

source_support.label: Britannica sword
source_support.support_summary: Supports sword equipment context for blades, hilts, and scabbard-related weapon carrying.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: upper metal or leather mouth fitting
angled straps connecting scabbard to belt

craft_sequence: Build long tapered scabbard body first.
Add throat and chape as separate named fittings.
Place hanger straps and belt loops at a declared angle.
Use rivets and material slots to identify guard, noble, or rogue variants.
Declare weapon socket separately from sheath geometry.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The scabbard hangs from belt or baldric; hanger angle and weapon socket are the functional facts.
operator_checks: Does the empty scabbard still read as weapon suspension?
Are hanger angle and weapon socket explicit?
Are throat and chape separate material parts?

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names throat, chape, hanger strap, belt loop, and weapon socket.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: A missing blade leaves its shape behind in leather.

source_support.label: Britannica eyeglasses
source_support.support_summary: Supports eyeglasses/spectacles as optical devices with lenses and frames.

source_support.label: The Met collection, spectacles references
source_support.support_summary: Supports visible reference variety for spectacle frames and cases.

craft_sequence: Build the case as the low-risk base object.
Add spectacles as paired rims and bridge, with lenses optional.
Use small material slots for glass, metal, case, and lining.
Declare lens/puzzle socket separately from decorative case geometry.
Keep high-detail frames optional for low-compute scenes.
accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: Spectacles are tiny readable props; the case protects them and can carry the interaction socket.
operator_checks: Does the case read even if spectacles are hidden?
Are lenses optional for low compute?
Is the lens/puzzle socket source-owned?

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Names lens rim, lens, bridge, case body, hinge, and lens socket.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: The lens does not make knowledge; it only refuses to let age hide it.

source_support.label: Britannica ring
source_support.support_summary: Supports signet/seal-bearing personal objects and authority/identity use.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: interaction target for wax seal gameplay

materials: bronze, iron, silver-like, or brass-like metal

accessory_items.attachment_mechanics: The seal matrix is a small authority object; its stamp face connects prop, document, and faction identity.
operator_checks: Is the stamp face clearly front/down-facing?
Is the identity mark source-owned?
Can wax/document interaction use the same source id?

lore_book_hooks.book_title: The Face That Writes in Wax

source_support.support_summary: Supports carried accessory context for wearable or portable personal objects.

anatomy_parts.geometry_role: edge stitching or stitched leather joint

Use patches and dents for traveler or ruin variants.

operator_checks: Does it read as a container before texture?
